node.title: A=1 shape-A tensor-rank-three projective-frame router
node.closure: rank three forces four general-position rows with a triple-free slope incidence frame
node.statement: Retain an official Shape-A all-excess survivor and suppose its biform G has tensor separation rank exactly three. In a minimal representation G=sum_(j=0)^2 A_j(t)B_j(X), the projective coefficient map b(x)=[B_0(x):B_1(x):B_2(x)] places at most n domain rows on any projective line. Since R=3n+7, there are four domain rows whose b-images are in general position, with at least seven choices for the fourth after the first three. Their four degree-m split row polynomials form a four-term circuit with every coefficient nonzero. No off-line slope can root three of them, since the circuit would root the fourth and three independent coefficient rows would make the complete parameter fiber zero. Hence every slope occurs in at most two of the four root sets; at least e-8 slopes occur in exactly two, and some row pair shares at least ceil((e-8)/6)=30541989660 official roots. Thus every survivor either has tensor rank at least four or contains this explicit rank-three frame.
